primary.title: Cyclone Arnab Tracker live: Current location
primary.description: Cyclone Arnab is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast near Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, by the forenoon of October 28, prompting evacuations and emergency preparations in coastal areas. The storm is forecast to bring strong winds, heavy rainfall and rough seas to parts of the east coast, while its wider weather impact is expected to extend to West Bengal, Odisha and Jharkhand.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the system was moving west-northwestwards over the west-central Bay of Bengal on Tuesday, October 27, after intensifying from a severe cyclonic storm into a very severe cyclonic storm. Authorities in Andhra Pradesh have stepped up preparedness, with more than 1,300 pregnant women shifted to hospitals and transport services affected as the cyclone approaches.Andhra Pradesh prepares for severe cyclone Arnab’s landfallThe IMD forecast that Arnab would cross the coast near Yanam by the forenoon of October 28. Depending on the bulletin cited, the storm’s forecast maximum sustained wind speeds range from 115-125 kmph, with gusts of up to 140 kmph, to a peak of 135 kmph with gusts reaching 150 kmph. Residents should follow the latest official IMD updates as the system approaches land, as reported by PTI.The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority has warned of heavy rainfall in northern coastal districts. Strong winds have already begun affecting coastal areas, including Visakhapatnam and Kakinada, while Srikakulam is expected to experience heavy rain accompanied by strong winds.In Kakinada district, rising sea waves have reached coastal areas around Uppada, Konapapet and Moolapet. Rough sea conditions have disrupted traffic between Uppada and Kakinada, raising concerns among residents of nearby settlements.The IMD has also warned that a storm surge of around 1 to 1.5 metres above the astronomical tide could inundate low-lying areas during landfall, with the highest peak surge expected near Kakinada and Yanam.Also Read: Weather today: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana receive heavy rainfall alert as Cyclone Arnab intensifies; check latest IMD updateWhere will Cyclone Arnab make landfall?According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), very severe cyclonic storm Arnab is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts near Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, by the forenoon of Wednesday, October 28. The storm is forecast to bring maximum sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, with gusts reaching 140 kmph. The IMD has also warned of a possible storm surge that could inundate low-lying coastal areas, particularly near Kakinada and Yanam.Where is the current location of very severe cyclone Arnab?According to the IMD bulletin issued early on Tuesday, October 27, Cyclone Arnab was located over the west-central Bay of Bengal, approximately 300 km southeast of Visakhapatnam, 360 km east-southeast of Kakinada, 380 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha, 460 km east of Machilipatnam and 530 km east of Bapatla. The storm was moving west-northwestwards and was expected to turn northwestwards as it approached the coast.— ANI (@ANI) Flights cancelled and railway tracks placed under surveillanceThe cyclone has begun affecting transport services in Andhra Pradesh. Two IndiGo flights connecting Vijayawada with Chennai and Bengaluru were cancelled on Tuesday because of the weather system.Railway authorities have placed around 600 km of track under close surveillance ahead of the expected landfall. Safety protocols and rapid restoration measures have been arranged across the Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam divisions.War rooms have also been activated at zonal, divisional and Railway Board levels to monitor conditions around the clock, with passenger safety identified as the priority.West Bengal likely to receive rain until October 30The effects of cyclone Arnab are also being felt in West Bengal, where coastal areas experienced moderate rainfall on Tuesday. The IMD has forecast moderate rain across all districts of South Bengal until October 29, with heavy rainfall possible in some districts through October 30.South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur recorded moderate rainfall on Tuesday, while some areas of Jhargram, Paschim Medinipur, Howrah and Kolkata also received rain.Kolkata is likely to experience light to moderate rainfall over the next two days. In the sub-Himalayan region, heavy rain is forecast in Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Alipurduar and Jalpaiguri on October 29 and 30.The weather department has advised fisherfolk not to venture into the sea until October 29. Squally conditions, with wind speeds of 40-50 kmph and occasional gusts of up to 60 kmph, are likely in the region.Odisha identifies 15,000 people for possible evacuationOdisha has begun preparations for possible weather impacts from the cyclone. In Gajapati district, authorities have identified 15,000 vulnerable people for evacuation and arranged 281 cyclone and temporary shelters, district collector Akshay Sunil Agrawal said, according to ANI.Agrawal said preparations had begun two days earlier. The district was under an orange warning for October 27 and 28, followed by a red warning for October 28 and 29.The state government has also announced the closure of schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts on October 28 and 29 because of the forecast heavy rainfall. District collectors will decide on closures elsewhere based on local conditions.Jharkhand issues yellow and orange alertsThe IMD has issued a yellow alert for Ranchi, Khunti, Simdega, Gumla, Lohardaga, Saraikela-Kharsawan, East Singhbhum and West Singhbhum. The alert is in effect for 24 hours from 8.30 am on October 28, according to a PTI report quoting officials.An orange alert has also been issued for Garhwa, Palamu, Latehar, Lohardaga, Gumla, Simdega and West Singhbhum. It remains in force until 8.30 am on October 30, according to the report.The Jharkhand government has asked district administrations to remain vigilant as heavy rainfall is expected in parts of the state over three days.Uttar Pradesh prepares for rain and thunderstormsUttar Pradesh authorities have issued precautionary guidelines ahead of forecasts of rain, thunderstorms and strong winds in parts of the state between October 28 and 31, ANI reported.A yellow alert has been issued for Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, Chandauli, Varanasi, Bhadohi, Ghazipur and Ballia, where winds of 30-40 kmph are expected on October 28. Officials have been directed to remain prepared for relief and rescue operations.As severe cyclone Arnab approaches the Andhra Pradesh coast, residents in potentially affected areas should monitor official weather bulletins and follow instructions issued by local administrations.

Safety protocols and rapid restoration measures have been arranged across the Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam divisions.War rooms have also been activated at zonal, divisional and Railway Board levels to monitor conditions around the clock, with passenger safety identified as the priority.West Bengal likely to receive rain until October 30The effects of cyclone Arnab are also being felt in West Bengal, where coastal areas experienced moderate rainfall on Tuesday. The IMD has forecast moderate rain across all districts of South Bengal until October 29, with heavy rainfall possible in some districts through October 30.South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur recorded moderate rainfall on Tuesday, while some areas of Jhargram, Paschim Medinipur, Howrah and Kolkata also received rain.Kolkata is likely to experience light to moderate rainfall over the next two days. In the sub-Himalayan region, heavy rain is forecast in Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Alipurduar and Jalpaiguri on October 29 and 30.The weather department has advised fisherfolk not to venture into the sea until October 29. Squally conditions, with wind speeds of 40-50 kmph and occasional gusts of up to 60 kmph, are likely in the region.Odisha identifies 15,000 people for possible evacuationOdisha has begun preparations for possible weather impacts from the cyclone. In Gajapati district, authorities have identified 15,000 vulnerable people for evacuation and arranged 281 cyclone and temporary shelters, district collector Akshay Sunil Agrawal said, according to ANI.Agrawal said preparations had begun two days earlier. The district was under an orange warning for October 27 and 28, followed by a red warning for October 28 and 29.The state government has also announced the closure of schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts on October 28 and 29 because of the forecast heavy rainfall. District collectors will decide on closures elsewhere based on local conditions.Jharkhand issues yellow and orange alertsThe IMD has issued a yellow alert for Ranchi, Khunti, Simdega, Gumla, Lohardaga, Saraikela-Kharsawan, East Singhbhum and West Singhbhum. The alert is in effect for 24 hours from 8.30 am on October 28, according to a PTI report quoting officials.An orange alert has also been issued for Garhwa, Palamu, Latehar, Lohardaga, Gumla, Simdega and West Singhbhum. It remains in force until 8.30 am on October 30, according to the report.The Jharkhand government has asked district administrations to remain vigilant as heavy rainfall is expected in parts of the state over three days.Uttar Pradesh prepares for rain and thunderstormsUttar Pradesh authorities have issued precautionary guidelines ahead of forecasts of rain, thunderstorms and strong winds in parts of the state between October 28 and 31, ANI reported.A yellow alert has been issued for Sonbhadra, Mirzapur, Chandauli, Varanasi, Bhadohi, Ghazipur and Ballia, where winds of 30-40 kmph are expected on October 28. Officials have been directed to remain prepared for relief and rescue operations.As severe cyclone Arnab approaches the Andhra Pradesh coast, residents in potentially affected areas should monitor official weather bulletins and follow instructions issued by local administrations.
